correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs every arc. Fixed-point-freeness gives trivial center and hypercenter. For an outside target \(y\), the map \(a\mapsto[a,y]\) is an endomorphism of the finite abelian kernel with trivial kernel \(C_K(y)\), hence an automorphism; therefore a kernel-origin Engel commutator cannot die. For an outside source and kernel target, the first commutator is a nontrivial kernel element and the second vanishes because the kernel is abelian, giving exact depth two. Since the quotient is cyclic, outside-outside commutators lie in the kernel and can vanish under iteration exactly when the elements already commute; the outside centralizer is the unique cyclic conjugate complement containing the target. These facts prove the component partition and all formulas. The packaged finite replay was inspected as corroboration only, not as the universal proof.

value.rationale: Frobenius groups are singled out by the foundational connectivity theorem as the principal soluble obstruction to strong connectivity. Replacing that qualitative obstruction by the complete directed graph, exact Engel depth, condensation, degrees, and arc count on a broad natural family is a substantive structural refinement rather than an isolated computation.

final_claim: For every finite Frobenius group \(G=K\rtimes C_m\) with nontrivial abelian kernel \(K\), the directed Engel graph on non-hypercentral elements equals its 2-Engel graph; its strong components are \(K^\#\) and the \(|K|\) conjugate-complement blocks, with every intercomponent arc directed from a complement block to the kernel block, yielding the stated underlying join graph, degrees, diameter, and arc count.
limitations: The kernel must be abelian and the complement cyclic.
Nonabelian kernels or noncyclic complements can have different internal Engel structure.
